{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: MyGet
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
  workflow_dispatch:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: pwsh
    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: Set VERSION_SUFFIX
      if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}
      run: echo "VERSION_SUFFIX=$Env:GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER" >> $Env:GITHUB_ENV
    - name: .NET Action
      uses: ./.github/actions/dotnet
    - name: Push
      env:
        MYGET_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MYGET_API_KEY }}
      run: dotnet nuget push "./artifacts/*.nupkg" -k $Env:MYGET_API_KEY -s https://www.myget.org/F/disqord/api/v3/index.json --skip-duplicate",
  "rationale": "The workflow has a single build job with no job timeout, so a hung dotnet restore/build or NuGet push could consume runner time indefinitely. Repository CI history shows successful runs completing in roughly 1-2 minutes, which is representative history supporting a bounded timeout with headroom. Adding timeout-minutes: 5 to the build job bounds runaway consumption while preserving every existing step, trigger, permission, secret usage, and network target. This matches the P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) and P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT pattern (derive timeout candidates from successful history), both with measured_ci_workflow_on_fork evidence scope. No permissions are weakened, no privileged actions or new secrets are added, and no new network access is introduced.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8", "experiment:batch-ishara-pattern-bat-a14b642d809bf336"]
}
